title: LightmapGI bakes incorrect indirect light inside opaque double-sided geometry
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
- 4.8.dev, master 39216f0c8
- 4.7.2.stable

Historical comparison:
- 4.3.stable does not show the same behavior in an equivalent synthetic scene (not the MRP, see "Additional information").

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) 12 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (RKL GT1) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-11400 @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 31.14 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

The issue was also reproduced on master 39216f0c8 on Windows 11.

### Issue description

LightmapGI bakes indirect environment light into geometry that is fully enclosed inside an opaque double-sided volume.

The MRP contains two identical closed opaque boxes, each with a smaller cube inside:

- one box uses `CULL_DISABLED`;
- the other uses the default `CULL_BACK` as a control.

There are no lights in the scene. The only illumination is the LightmapGI environment, using a white custom color.

The outer boxes are hidden from the camera for clarity, but they still participate in the LightmapGI bake.

The denoiser is disabled.

After baking on master 39216f0c8, the cube inside the `CULL_DISABLED` box is clearly illuminated, while the equivalent `CULL_BACK` control remains almost black.

The enclosed cube has no visibility to the environment, so this lighting is invalid.

The cause appears to be in `trace_ray()` in `modules/lightmapper_rd/lm_compute.glsl`.

`trace_ray()` applies the material cull mode before returning whether the hit was on the geometric front or back.

For `CULL_DISABLED` materials, a geometric back-face hit is therefore reported as `RAY_FRONT` and the geometric side of the hit is lost.

During baking this causes two problems:

- the unocclude pass checks for `RAY_BACK` to detect texels located inside geometry; with `CULL_DISABLED` it never sees a geometric back face;
- indirect bounce rays that hit the inside of opaque double-sided geometry are shaded as front-face hits, using the outward-facing side of the triangle, so the bounce can leave the volume and collect environment light that the enclosed texel cannot see.

The per-triangle cull mode was added to the lightmapper in #99538 together with transparency support.

The transparency support itself is not the problem.

The issue is that geometric hit side and material cull behavior are combined too early in `trace_ray()`.

glTF materials with `doubleSided: true` are imported as `CULL_DISABLED`, so imported geometry using that material configuration can be affected without manually changing the cull mode.

A proposed fix is available in PR #123713:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123713

The proposed fix keeps the geometric hit side separate from the material cull mode while preserving the existing transparency behavior.

![master 39216f0c8, the same commit with #123713 applied, and the absolute difference x4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samjanny/godot-lightmap-backface-mrp/main/docs/before_after_pr123713.png)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Download or clone the MRP:
   https://github.com/samjanny/godot-lightmap-backface-mrp
2. Open the project in Godot.
3. Open `main.tscn` if needed.
4. Select the `LightmapGI` node and bake the lightmaps.
5. Accept the suggested `main.lmbake` path.
6. Run the project.
7. Compare the two enclosed cubes.

Expected:

Both enclosed cubes should remain almost black because both are inside closed opaque volumes with no internal light source and no visibility to the environment.

Actual:

The cube inside the `CULL_DISABLED` volume receives strong baked indirect/environment light, while the `CULL_BACK` control remains almost black.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

https://github.com/samjanny/godot-lightmap-backface-mrp

The MRP contains only the minimal project files required for reproduction plus the comparison image in `docs/`.

It does not use custom engine code or instrumentation.

### Additional information

In the MRP:

- master 39216f0c8: the `CULL_DISABLED` cube is visibly lit;
- 4.7.2.stable: `CULL_DISABLED` cube mean about 0.589, `CULL_BACK` cube mean about 0.0033.

A separate synthetic scene was also used during investigation. That scene is not the MRP.

It contains a small cube fully enclosed in opaque geometry, a white environment, an omni light outside the enclosing geometry, and has the denoiser disabled.

Saved measurements from that synthetic scene (mean L0 of the enclosed cube):

| Build | Material | Mean L0 |
|---|---|---|
| master e2b42469 | `CULL_DISABLED` | 0.789 |
| master e2b42469 + #123713 | `CULL_DISABLED` | 0.024 |
| 4.3.stable | `CULL_DISABLED` | 0.008 |
| master e2b42469 | `CULL_BACK` control | 0.006 |

PR #123713 was also regression-tested against the modern transparency path. Existing test results:

- transparent glass: bit-identical master vs fix;
- colored transparent glass: bit-identical;
- two transparent surfaces in sequence: bit-identical;
- alpha/cutout transmission is preserved.
